findings.reason: a node dispatched on §18 re-implements landed work, and its declared negative control ("restore the second resolver") would re-add the resolver that commit removed, turning a completed section into a regression.
findings.text: §18's done-when and its opening paragraph are written against `dispatch._fleet_record_path` (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py`, about line 9614), which no longer exists: commit d9b3b1a714 (2026-10-27, "fix(crew): read the fleet record where its owner publishes it") deleted the duplicate resolver and its dispatch re-export, made `_read_fleet_record` ask `fleet_supervisor.state_directory()`, and added `tests/test_dispatch_reads_the_fleet_record_through_its_owner.py` — which is exactly §18's done-when — yet `plan-section-declarations` still reads `s18: implementable` and the plan records neither the commit nor the landing

findings.reason: §9 is declared `done` on a gate a later reader cannot open, so an auditor resolving the section's evidence finds a miss and cannot tell a landed section from a lost one.

findings.reason: without a control the node cannot show that its new module boundary is load-bearing, so the section can close on a move that changes no behaviour and proves nothing.
findings.text: §17 declares no negative control; its only measure is "the population of test files importing `reckon.crew.dispatch` adds no failure against base", a delta that a refactor leaving the supervisor behaviour unreachable would still satisfy

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — three of the four sections still to be built cite a symbol, module or line that no longer exists, and §9's done-when names a test file that was never created.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §17's only measure is a population no-added-failure delta against base, with no negative control at all, so its gate cannot show the guard fires.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every landed section cites a durable path (`docs/research/data/dispatch-lifetime.json`, `docs/evidence/archive/a-dispatch-returns-without-its-worker-landed.html#s2/#s5/#s7/#s10`, figures under `docs/figures/a-dispatch-returns-without-its-worker/`), and all four anchors resolve; the open sections name no path, and the archive convention those landed sections establish is where their evidence would go.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no symbol, file or comment the plan instructs carries a plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag; plan-name references (`worker-death-is-recorded`, `a-follower-keeps-your-work-in-view`) are prose cross-references, not code names.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §16's section text states a mechanism (a pointer written before admission is decided) that the plan's own later correction refutes (the release exists; the plan branch returns before it), and §10's declared status contradicts its own recorded evidence.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §10's done-when spans a dotfiles change, five reckon launch behaviours and an on-node `scancel` proof, so one verdict cannot close it.
